FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 February 1979, after the draft finalized by the Builder's Hardware Sectional Committee had been a pproved by the Civ,l Engineering DIvision Council.

0.2 Rising butt hinges are used for fixing the door shutters to the frame
when it is intended that the shutters get automatically closed. When the ,.
door is opened, the flap of the hinge fixed to the shutter, spu"ally over the other flap fixed to the frame, elevates the shutter, The door gets automa-

tically closed when the flap of the hinge by way of its own weight and
weight of the shutter tends to move down spirally. These hinges find

their use when the door shutters are not up to the full height of the
opening, such as doors for cabins of doctors, station officers of police or radway stations or COT other offices where considerable public dealings are

involved.

0.3 This standard contains clauses 5.1 and 6.3 which permit the purchaser to use his options for selection to suit his requirements.
0.4 In formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries, in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in
this country.

0.5 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on builder's hardware. Other standards published so far in the series are given at page 13.

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated express-

ing tlt'e result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this

standard.
"Rules for rounding off numerical values ("vued).

5. CONSTRUCTION
5.1 General- The ri'ing butt hinges shall comply with Fig. I to 3, lead wah Tables 2 to 4.
NOTE - The purchaser. when ordering, should state the hand of r ismg butt hinges Handing of rHlng butt hmgp.q ~haJi be determined by the handing of the door on which It IS fitted The lunge is termed' left-hand' If It is fitted to left-hand door, and' right-hand' If it is fitted to rIght-hand door.

5.2 Pins - Pins shall be made of steel wire for all types of rising butt hinges. The pins shall be firmly fixed except that the steel butt hinges may also be supplied with loose headed pms, In case of brass lunges the pins shall be flush with 'he ends of the hmges as shown 10 Fig. 3. 5.3 The helix and the linings of knuckles of bra" rising butt hinges shall be of mild steel.
5.4 Screw Holes - All screw holes sha II be countersunk.
5.4.1 The screw holes shall be suitable for countersunk head wood screw conforrnmg to IS : 6i6u-19i~' and of the sizes speufied in Tables 2 to 4 lor different types and sizes of hmges, The SIze of the hules shall be such that when it IS countersunk it shall be able to accommodate the full depth of countersunk head of the wood screw specified.

5.4.2 Number of Holes - The number of holes shall be as specified in Tables 2 to 4.
� Speczficatton foc slotted countersunk head wood screws.

IS I 9106 � 1979

5.4.3 Position oj Holes - When more than two screw holes are provided in each flap they shall he distributed in zig-zag manner as shown in Fig. I to 3 but shall be equidistant from one another. The mirnmum clear distance of the screw holes from the end of the flap either parallel to the pin or across it shall be as follows:
Xor

r
Not less than 5 mm Not less than 7 mm

For hinges of 75 mm and 100 mm sizes For hinges of 125 mm size

.z

For all sizes of hinges Not less than 4 mm where X = distance of the end hole from the end of flap measured parallel to the pin; r = distance of the end hole from the end of flap measured at right angles to the pin; and

Z=

distance of the end of hole nearest to knuckle edge, where

holes are provided m zig-zag manner, from the edge of the knuckle slot.

6. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH
6.1 Hinges shall be well made and shall be free from /laws and defects. 6.2 Movement - The movement of the lunge shall be firm and easy to operate when fitted. 6.3 Unless specified otherwise, the hinges shall be finished bright with
smooth surfaces The brass hinges shall have bright or satin finish and

shall be suitably protected agamst drscolourauon.

7. MARKING
7.1 Each hinge sball be legibly and indelibly marked with the name of manufacturer or trade-mark, if any. 7.1.1 The hinge may also be marked with the lSI Certification Mark.
NOTE - The use of the lSI Certrficanon Mark is governed by the provlslons of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The lSI Mark On products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection. testmg and quality control which is devised and supervised by lSI and operated by the producer. lSI marked products are also contmuousl y checked by lSI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence [or the use of the lSI Cerrrficatron Mark may be granted to manufacturers Or proce!l!lOr!l, may be obtained from the Indian Standards. Institution.

A-2.2 Sample Size - Rising butt hinges for testing shall be selected at random from at least 10 percent of the packages subject to a minimum of three packages, equal number of hinges being selected from each such package.
~3. .TESTS

A-3.1 All rising butt hinges as selected as given in A-2.1 and A-2.2 shall
be checked for dimensions subject to tolerances. defects in manufacture,

and finish. Any hinge which fails to satisfy these requirements shall be considered as defecuve hinge.

A-i. CRITERION FOR CONFORMITY A-i.l A lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of this standard jf the number of defective hinges among those tested does nOI
exceed the corresponding number given in col 3 of Table 6.
